counterfactual_missing_items: No blood culture growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa is reported
No mention of characteristic skin lesion eponym 'ecthyma gangrenosum' in the vignette
No direct microbiologic confirmation of Pseudomonas species
decisive_items: Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
response.rationale: R3 (Ecthyma gangrenosum) is the most specific and clinically integrated diagnosis, directly matching the skin lesions, histopathology, and immunocompromised context. R1 (Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection) is the underlying etiology but is a broader diagnosis; R3 is the precise cutaneous manifestation. Other candidates are either too generic (R2), incorrect organism (R4), or non-diagnostic (R5).

rejected.why: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection is the underlying cause but not the most specific diagnosis; ecthyma gangrenosum is the characteristic skin manifestation.
Neutropenic sepsis is too broad and does not account for the specific skin and histopathologic findings.
Bacillus anthracis infection is not supported; the clinical picture and gram-variable rods are more consistent with Pseudomonas, and anthrax would have different epidemiology and morphology.
Necrotizing fasciitis is a deep soft-tissue infection; the findings are localized to skin with vesicles and necrosis, not fascial necrosis.
This is a completion of R1 adding 'in neutropenic patient' but does not add diagnostic specificity beyond the underlying infection.
This is a completion of R3 adding 'of skin' which is redundant and does not change the diagnosis.
